archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose floor comes from improvised scrambles rather than designed runs. His passing value comes from throws at 10+ air yards, not from the quick game.

report.headline: Sharper passer, same scrambling engine, but sacks and third downs still cap him.
report.take:
Daniels in 2026 is closer to the rookie who ranked 9th in EPA per play than to the player who slid in an injury-shortened 2025. The clearest sign is accuracy. His CPOE of 4.9 ranks 10th of 47, a swing of 7.6 points from last year's -2.7, and his bad-throw rate fell 3.5 points. He hasn't thrown an interception in five games. The legs are still the separator: 47.2 rushing yards a game leads all qualifiers, and nearly all of it comes from scrambles. He has 21 scrambles for 235 yards and 11 first downs at 0.857 EPA each. His four designed runs have produced nothing.

The passing profile is split down the middle. Throws of 10+ air yards are worth 0.467 EPA an attempt, 22.9 EPA in total. The intermediate area has been outstanding, with a 17.7 CPOE on 27 attempts. Everything under 10 yards nets slightly negative, dragged down by a screen game that has cost 9.8 EPA on 16 throws behind the line. So the offense works when he pushes the ball outside the numbers and when he extends plays. It stalls when the plan is quick and horizontal.

The number that hides the most is the sack rate. It is 7.6% for the season and 10.5% over the last three games, and 11 of his 12 sacks came in that stretch. That isn't the old habit coming back. His pressure-to-sack rate of 30.3% is far better than the 41-44% marks of his first two years. The issue is volume of pressure: Washington's offensive hit rate ranks 26th, and Laremy Tunsil hasn't played a snap. Third down is where it shows most. He has 7 sacks on 44 third-down plays, -0.235 EPA, and a 31.8% conversion rate facing an average of 8 yards to go.

Going forward, the accuracy gains look real because they match his rookie baseline, and the rushing is a multi-year trait. The zero interceptions will not hold for a player who threw 9 as a rookie. The receiver room just got thinner. Terry McLaurin (0.661 EPA per target) is done for the year with a torn patellar tendon, and Jaylin Lane is also on IR. That leaves Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who has been the most efficient target at 0.937 EPA, carrying the downfield work.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for everything
strengths.body: He leads all qualifiers in rushing yards per game, and the source is improvisation. He scrambles on 11.8% of dropbacks at 0.857 EPA per scramble, with 11 first downs. He finished second in QB rushing as a rookie, so this is his identity, not a hot streak.

strengths.title: Accuracy back to rookie form
strengths.body: CPOE has jumped 7.6 points from last season to rank 10th, and it has run hotter lately at 8.1 over the last three games. That includes a 17.6 mark on 40 attempts against a San Francisco defense ranked 8th. Because it matches his 2024 level rather than appearing from nowhere, it should mostly hold.

strengths.title: Value lives at 10+ air yards
strengths.body: Throws of 10 or more air yards produce 0.467 EPA an attempt. The 10-19 yard window has been especially strong, with a 63% completion rate and 0.63 success. This is the passing offense's real engine. The intermediate CPOE comes from 27 attempts, so it is a hint more than a fact.

concerns.title: Sacks climbing behind a leaky line
concerns.body: His sack rate is 10.5% over the last three games, and the line allows the 26th-ranked hit rate with Tunsil on IR until at least late December. His pressure-to-sack rate is actually much better than in past years, so this is mostly a protection problem. That also means it won't fix itself until the line does.

concerns.title: Third downs and the quick game
concerns.body: Third down has cost 10.3 EPA, with 7 sacks and a 31.8% conversion rate at 8 yards to go on average. Those are long-yardage situations that the protection can't hold up in. The screen and behind-the-line game has been a second leak. His short work overall sits near zero, meaning drives depend on his legs or a downfield completion.

concerns.title: Lost his best vertical options
concerns.body: McLaurin produced 0.661 EPA per target before his season-ending knee surgery, and Lane is also out for the year. Diggs and Antonio Williams have been efficient, but the depth chart behind them is Burks and Okonkwo. Neither has topped 0.19 EPA per target.

trend.note: His accuracy has sharpened across the last three games: 7.62 YPA and 8.1 CPOE, with a 300-yard day at San Francisco. A rising sack rate has cancelled most of it, leaving EPA per dropback slightly below his season mark.

nextGame.headline: Rams take away the deep ball but rarely get home
nextGame.body:
The Rams' defense ranks 4th in EPA and has been the stingiest in the league on deep passes. That points straight at Daniels' best passing zone. They are also 5th against short throws, so there is no easy underneath alternative, which is already his weak spot. The opening is protection. The Rams rank 29th in hit rate and 27th in sack rate, which is the softest pass rush he's seen in weeks. Cleaner pockets could cut into the sacks that have stalled recent drives, and he could attack the intermediate range if he isn't forced to escape. Washington is a 5.5-point home underdog. If they trail, his trailing-by-9+ numbers have been good (0.192 EPA, 15.2 CPOE).

Availability matters on both sides. Myles Garrett is on IR but reportedly on track to practice. If he plays, the Rams' weak pass-rush numbers stop being reliable against a Washington line without Tunsil. Corners Trent McDuffie (back) and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) are both questionable, and losing either would loosen a secondary that has been strong on the outside. On Washington's side, McLaurin is out, so Diggs and Antonio Williams must win outside against that coverage. Matthew Stafford's arm soreness could also change the game script if it limits the Rams' pass-leaning offense.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield game vs the best deep defense
keyMatchups.body: Most of Daniels' passing EPA comes from 10+ air yards, and the Rams allow the fewest EPA on deep throws in the league. If they take that away, he needs intermediate completions and scrambles to carry the offense.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Rams rush vs leaky line
keyMatchups.body: The Rams rank near the bottom in both hit rate and sack rate. Daniels' sack troubles come from pressure volume, not holding the ball, so this is the matchup most likely to calm them, unless Garrett returns.

keyMatchups.title: Tight end lane mostly closed
keyMatchups.body: The Rams have held top tight ends 4.4 PPR under their averages, 2nd-best in the league. That squeezes Okonkwo, his second-most targeted receiver. Their weak spot has been WR3s, which points to Burks as a possible outlet.

nextGame.watch: Whether Myles Garrett is active. Without him, Daniels should finally get clean pockets; with him, the sack problem likely continues.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts most likely to last are the rushing and the accuracy. He led the league in QB rushing pace and finished second as a rookie, and his CPOE is back near his 2024 level. Expect roughly 190-235 passing yards and 38-55 rushing yards a game, a weekly PPR floor in the high teens, and upside when the scrambles pile up. The zero interceptions will not last for a passer who threw 9 as a rookie. His touchdown rate, 27th of 47, has some room to rise given his rookie track record.

The ceiling depends on protection and receivers. Tunsil's possible late-December return is the one clear upgrade on the horizon. Until then, the sack rate and third-down struggles are structural. McLaurin's loss puts more downfield volume on Diggs and Antonio Williams, and Williams' 0.937 EPA per target on 18 looks is a small sample likely to cool.
swingFactors: Diggs and Antonio Williams holding up without McLaurin

confidence.note: Five games played plus a thinning receiver room. His career baseline steadies the accuracy and rushing read.
